Seek Inspiration depends on what is on top of your deck, and it does nothing if the card is not a qualifying Pokémon. Super Psy Bolt is the steady backup. The Slowking deck plays three in every top list. Its Retreat Cost of 3 makes it slow to move out of the Active Spot.
Slowpoke: Slowpoke is a Basic Psychic Pokémon with 80 HP that evolves into Slowking. Decks play it to get there. Dangle Tail costs one Colorless Energy and puts a Pokémon from your discard pile into your hand, and Tackle does 30 damage.

The Slowking deck plays four in every top list. Slowking's Seek Inspiration discards cards from the top of your deck, so Dangle Tail can bring back a Pokémon that ended up in the discard pile that way.
Solrock: Solrock is a Basic Fighting Pokémon with one attack, Cosmic Beam. For a single Fighting Energy it does 70 damage, and Weakness and Resistance don't change that number. The catch is that the attack does nothing unless you have Lunatone on your Bench.

Every top list for Lucario Hariyama, Okidogi Barbaracle, Mega Lucario and Ceruledge plays it, usually two or three copies. RdyDeck's Mega Lucario guide notes that Solrock also turns on Lunar Cycle, so plan to have Lunatone on the Bench beside it. Its Retreat Cost of 1 keeps it easy to move.
Special Red Card: Special Red Card is an Item that disrupts your opponent's hand late in the game. Your opponent shuffles their hand, puts it on the bottom of their deck, and draws 3 new cards. A big hand they built up is gone, and they are left with 3 cards to work with.

You can play it only once your opponent has 3 or fewer Prize cards left, so it waits in your hand early on. If their hand is empty, they draw nothing. Most decks run a single copy, including Dragapult Dusknoir, Grimmsnarl Froslass, Mega Rayquaza and Lopunny Dusknoir. Alakazam Dusknoir plays it in every top list, usually 2.
Spiky Energy: Spiky Energy is a Special Energy that counts as one Colorless Energy. When the Pokémon it is attached to is in the Active Spot and takes damage from your opponent's attack, the attacking Pokémon gets 2 damage counters, even if your Pokémon is Knocked Out.

That puts a cost on every attack into your Active Pokémon. It only works in the Active Spot and only against damage from attacks, so it does nothing on the Bench. Crustle plays it in nearly every top list and Toucannon in most, both usually 4 copies. Iron Thorns plays it less often, usually 2.
Strange Timepiece: Strange Timepiece is an Item that devolves one of your own evolved Psychic Pokémon. You take any number of the Evolution cards stacked on it back into your hand, and the Pokémon underneath stays in play.

Getting those Evolution cards back lets you play them again on a later turn. The devolved Pokémon can't evolve again the same turn, so plan for the Evolution cards to wait a turn in your hand. It only works on Psychic Pokémon. Alakazam Dusknoir is the one deck that plays it, in 91% of top lists, usually 3 copies.
Switch: Switch is an Item that swaps your Active Pokémon with one of your Benched Pokémon. You get the effect of retreating without paying any Retreat Cost, and since it is an Item you can play it in the same turn as your Supporter.

Decks use it to pull a damaged or trapped Pokémon out of the Active Spot, or to bring an attacker up. Lopunny Dusknoir leans on it most, usually 4 copies in nearly every top list. Mega Rayquaza usually plays 2, and Lucario Hariyama, Greninja, Cynthia's Garchomp and Hop's Trevenant usually play 1.
Talonflame ex: Talonflame ex is a Stage 2 Pokémon ex that evolves from Fletchinder, but its Excited Dive Ability lets you skip that. Once during your turn, if you have a Colorless Mega Evolution Pokémon ex in play, you can put Talonflame ex from your hand straight onto your Bench.

Its attack, Talon Hunt, costs two Colorless Energy, does 150 damage and lets you search your deck for up to 2 cards. It has no Retreat Cost, and as a Pokémon ex it gives up 2 Prize cards when Knocked Out. Talonflame Dusknoir plays 4 and Mega Rayquaza plays 2 in every top list, and Basic Box usually plays 1.
Tapu Bulu: Tapu Bulu is a Basic Grass Pokémon with one attack, Wood Hammer. It costs two Grass and two Colorless Energy and does 220 damage, then does 30 damage to Tapu Bulu itself.

The self-damage adds up across turns on its 140 HP, and its Retreat Cost of 3 makes it slow to move out of the Active Spot. It is also weak to Fire. Ogerpon Meganium Hydrapple is the one deck that plays it, as a single copy in about two thirds of its top lists.
Tasty Rice Ball: Tasty Rice Ball is an Item that heals 30 damage from your Active Pokémon. It gets stronger as you use more of them: it heals 30 more for each other Tasty Rice Ball already in your discard pile.

So the first one heals 30, the second 60, the third 90 and the fourth 120. It only heals the Active Pokémon, so it does nothing for damage on your Bench. Crustle is the one deck that plays it, in 60% of top lists, and those lists usually run 4 copies to get the most from the growing heal.
Tatsugiri: Tatsugiri is a Basic Dragon Pokémon played for its Attract Customers Ability. Once during your turn, while it is in the Active Spot, you look at the top 6 cards of your deck and take a Supporter from them into your hand. The rest are shuffled back in.

It only works from the Active Spot and can miss if no Supporter is in those 6 cards. Its Retreat Cost of 1 makes it easy to move after use, and its Surf attack does 50 for a Fire and a Water Energy. Sharpedo Toxtricity plays it in nearly every top list, usually 2, and Toucannon also usually plays 2. Mega Dragonite, Gengar, N's Zoroark and Grimmsnarl Froslass usually play 1.
Teal Mask Ogerpon ex: Teal Mask Ogerpon ex is a Basic Grass Pokémon ex. Its Teal Dance Ability lets you attach a Basic Grass Energy from your hand to it once during your turn, and then draw a card. Its attack, Myriad Leaf Shower, does 30 plus 30 more for each Energy on both Active Pokémon, so it hits harder as Energy builds up.

As a Tera Pokémon it takes no damage from attacks while on your Bench, but it gives up 2 Prize cards when Knocked Out. Every top list of its six decks plays it. Ogerpon Meganium Arboliva, Ogerpon Meganium Hydrapple and Mega Venusaur usually run 4, Raging Bolt Ogerpon 3, and Basic Box and Clefairy Ogerpon 2.
Team Rocket's Factory: Team Rocket's Factory is a Stadium that adds draw to Team Rocket Supporters. Once during each player's turn, if that player played a Supporter with Team Rocket in its name from their hand that turn, they may draw 2 cards.

It works for both players, so it only helps your opponent if they also play Team Rocket Supporters. Like any Stadium, it is discarded when another Stadium comes into play. Rocket's Honchkrow plays it in every top list, usually 3, while Rocket's Mewtwo and Rocket's Spidops usually play 2. Kangaskhan Bouffalant plays it less often but usually runs 3.
Team Rocket's Petrel: Team Rocket's Petrel is a Supporter that searches your deck for any one Trainer card and puts it into your hand. That can be the Item, Stadium, Pokémon Tool or Supporter your turn needs.

It uses your Supporter for the turn, so you trade drawing cards for one exact pick. Since it has Team Rocket in its name, it also counts for Team Rocket's Factory. Hop's Trevenant plays 4 in every top list, Grimmsnarl Froslass usually plays 2, and Sharpedo Toxtricity, Rocket's Mewtwo, Lucario Hariyama and Cynthia's Garchomp usually play 1.
Team Rocket's Watchtower: Team Rocket's Watchtower is a Stadium that turns off the Abilities of every Colorless Pokémon in play, yours and your opponent's. Decks play it to shut down Colorless Pokémon whose Abilities the other player relies on.

It hits your own Colorless Pokémon too, so check your list before you play it. It stays in play until another Stadium replaces it. N's Zoroark, Absol Audino and Sharpedo Toxtricity play it in more than 90% of top lists, usually 2. Dragapult Blaziken and Dragapult Dusknoir usually play 1, and Cynthia's Garchomp usually 2.
Telepathic Psychic Energy: Telepathic Psychic Energy is a Special Energy that counts as Psychic Energy. When you attach it from your hand to a Psychic Pokémon, you also search your deck for up to 2 Basic Psychic Pokémon and put them onto your Bench.

One attachment both powers a Pokémon and fills your Bench. The search only happens when you attach it from your hand, and only onto a Psychic Pokémon. Every deck that plays it runs 4 in nearly all of its top lists: Alakazam Dusknoir, Lopunny Dusknoir, Hop's Trevenant, Slowking, Alakazam Dudunsparce and Mega Chandelure.
Thwackey: Thwackey is a Stage 1 Grass Pokémon that evolves from Grookey. Its Boom Boom Groove Ability lets you search your deck for any one card once during your turn, as long as your Active Pokémon has the Festival Lead Ability.

Without a Festival Lead Pokémon in the Active Spot the Ability does nothing, so the decks that play it build around keeping one there. Seaking Festival Lead and Festival Lead both play 4 in every top list. Its own attack, Beat, does 50 for two Grass Energy.
Torchic: Torchic is a Basic Fire Pokémon that evolves into Combusken, and decks play it to start that evolution line. Its Collect attack draws a card for one Colorless Energy, and Combustion does 10 damage for one Fire Energy.

With 70 HP it is fragile, so it helps to get it onto your Bench early and evolve it soon. Collect gives you something useful to do if it starts in the Active Spot. Dragapult Blaziken plays 2 in every top list, and Mega Dragonite usually plays 3 in 91% of top lists.
Toxel: Toxel is a Basic Darkness Pokémon that evolves into Toxtricity, and decks play it to get there. Its Call for Family attack, for one Darkness Energy, searches your deck for up to 2 Basic Pokémon and puts them onto your Bench.

That makes it a useful Pokémon to have in the Active Spot early, since one attack can fill your Bench. Playful Kick does 20 for a Darkness and a Colorless Energy. Toxtricity Box plays 4 in every top list, Toxtricity plays 3, and Sharpedo Toxtricity, Gengar and Mega Darkrai usually play 2.
Toxtricity: Toxtricity is a Stage 1 Darkness Pokémon that evolves from Toxel. Its Sinister Surge Ability searches your deck for a Basic Darkness Energy once during your turn and attaches it to one of your Benched Darkness Pokémon, then puts 2 damage counters on that Pokémon.

The extra Energy comes with damage as its cost, and it can only go to a Benched Darkness Pokémon. RdyDeck's Sharpedo Toxtricity guide notes that those counters turn on Hungry Jaws. Toxtricity Box plays 4 in every top list, Toxtricity 3, and Sharpedo Toxtricity, Gengar and Mega Darkrai usually 2.
Ultra Ball: Ultra Ball is an Item that searches your deck for any Pokémon and puts it into your hand. To play it, you discard 2 other cards from your hand. Since it finds any Pokémon, it can get a Basic, an Evolution card or the attacker you need.

The 2-card discard is the price, so you need 2 other cards in hand to play it. Most decks that play it run 4: Dragapult Blaziken, Dragapult Dusknoir, Sharpedo Toxtricity, Lucario Hariyama and Mega Rayquaza usually play 4 in nearly every top list, and Dragapult usually plays 3.
Unfair Stamp: Unfair Stamp is an ACE SPEC Item for coming back after a Knock Out. You can play it only if one of your Pokémon was Knocked Out during your opponent's last turn. Both players shuffle their hands into their decks, then you draw 5 cards and your opponent draws 2.

That refreshes your hand and shrinks theirs at once. As an ACE SPEC it uses your deck's one ACE SPEC slot. Dragapult Blaziken, Dragapult and Ogerpon Meganium Arboliva play it in more than 95% of top lists, and Dragapult Dusknoir and Sharpedo Toxtricity in more than 80%. Lucario Hariyama plays it in half.
Wally's Compassion: Wally's Compassion is a Supporter that heals all damage from one of your Mega Evolution Pokémon ex. If it healed any damage, all Energy attached to that Pokémon goes back into your hand.

Losing the Energy from the Pokémon is the cost, but the cards stay in your hand to attach again. It only works on Mega Evolution Pokémon ex and uses your Supporter for the turn. Mega Starmie plays 4 in nearly every top list, Lopunny Dudunsparce usually 3, and Starmie Froslass usually 2. RdyDeck's Lopunny Dudunsparce guide uses it on Mega Lopunny ex.
Wellspring Mask Ogerpon ex: Wellspring Mask Ogerpon ex is a Basic Water Pokémon ex. Sob does 20 for one Energy and stops the Defending Pokémon from retreating during your opponent's next turn. Torrential Pump does 100, and you can shuffle 3 of its attached Energy into your deck to also do 120 to one of your opponent's Benched Pokémon.

Using that Bench damage means building its Energy up again afterward. As a Tera Pokémon it takes no damage from attacks on your Bench, but it gives up 2 Prize cards when Knocked Out. Most decks run 1, including Basic Box in every top list, while Mew Box and Lillie's Clefairy usually play 2.
Wondrous Patch: Wondrous Patch is an Item that takes a Basic Psychic Energy from your discard pile and attaches it to one of your Benched Psychic Pokémon. Decks use it to reuse discarded Energy and power up a Benched attacker.

It needs a Basic Psychic Energy already in your discard pile, and it can only target a Benched Psychic Pokémon, not your Active one. Special Energy such as Telepathic Psychic Energy can't be picked. Lillie's Clefairy plays 4 in every top list, and Slowking, Alakazam Dudunsparce and Mew Box usually play 3.
Xerosic's Machinations: Xerosic's Machinations is a Supporter that makes your opponent discard cards from their hand until they have 3 left. They choose which cards go, but a big hand gets cut down to 3.

It does nothing if your opponent already has 3 or fewer cards, and it uses your Supporter for the turn without drawing you any cards. Most decks run 1, including Absol Audino and Crustle in more than 90% of top lists and Mega Lopunny in 80%. Mega Chandelure usually plays 2.
Yveltal: Yveltal is a Basic Darkness Pokémon with no Retreat Cost. Clutch does 20 for one Darkness Energy and stops the Defending Pokémon from retreating during your opponent's next turn. Dark Feather does 110 for two Darkness and one Colorless Energy.

Clutch can keep a Pokémon stuck in the Active Spot for a turn, and the free retreat makes Yveltal easy to move in and out. Most decks run 1: Absol Audino plays it in 98% of top lists, Grimmsnarl Froslass in 89% and N's Zoroark in 70%. Mega Absol Box usually plays 2.
Zeraora: Zeraora is a Basic Lightning Pokémon with an attack aimed at Benched Pokémon ex. Thunder Raid costs three Lightning Energy, discards all Energy from Zeraora, and does 210 damage to one of your opponent's Benched Pokémon ex, with no Weakness or Resistance applied.

It only hits a Benched Pokémon ex, so it has no target if your opponent's Bench has none. Since it discards all its Energy, it must be powered up again before the next Thunder Raid. Scratch does 20 for one Energy. Slowking plays 1 in 69% of top lists, and Manectric Eelektrik plays 1 in 44%.
